Mermaid API · Open beta

# Let your agent draw. We make sure the diagram works.

Mermaid diagrams for your code, agents and products. One API call.

## One key, from code to collaboration

Validate

Check diagram code before anyone sees it. If it is broken, you get the line, the column and a stable error code your program can act on.

Render

Turn diagram code into SVG, PNG or PDF, with any Mermaid theme, look and layout, including Mermaid's own premium layouts.

Generate

Describe a diagram in plain language and get valid Mermaid code back. Every result is checked before it reaches you.

Repair

Send broken diagram code and get working code back, checked the same way.

Browse

Find your Mermaid Chart projects and diagrams, then fetch a diagram by ID with its code, version and edit URL.

Create

Save valid diagram code in Mermaid Chart, in your default project or a project you choose. Get a diagram ID and edit URL back.

Update

Change a stored diagram's code or title by ID. The API validates code before saving; the last write wins.

Share

Invite someone with a share link. Recipients must log in; links default to View, last 30 days and are not revocable before use.

## Where Mermaid API fits

AI agents and chat tools

Language models write Mermaid well, but not perfectly. Validate what your model produced before your user sees it, repair it when it breaks, and render it to an image your chat or app can show.

Docs and CI pipelines

Render the diagrams in your docs to SVG, PNG or PDF at build time. Validate them in CI and fail the build on a broken diagram, before it ships.

From program to teammate

Offer diagrams in your product without running a browser farm. Create a stored diagram, keep its ID for later updates, and hand an edit URL or share invitation to a teammate.

Diagrams from a description

Turn a sentence into a first draft. "Alice says hello to Bob, as a sequence diagram" becomes working Mermaid code, ready to render or refine.

## One request. A real answer.

bash

```
curl https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/render \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MERMAID_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"code": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B[Done]", "format": "svg"}' \
  -o diagram.svg
```

The response is the image itself, ready to write to disk.

## Mermaid is open source. Why use the API?

Nothing to host

Rendering Mermaid needs a headless browser. We run it, so you send one HTTP request.

Always the latest Mermaid

Including Mermaid's own layouts and themes, the day they ship.

Answers a program can use

Stable error codes with line and column, not a stack trace.

Built by the Mermaid team

The people who make Mermaid run the service.

## Built for programs, not people

Self-describing

An OpenAPI document and an llms.txt, so agents and code generators can find their own way around.

Stable error codes

Every failure has a documented code that will not change. Messages may improve; codes stay.

Pin your Mermaid version

Choose the Mermaid version a call uses, so a render does not change under you.

Know your balance

A free endpoint tells your program what it has left and what each call costs. Out of credits says "buy"; too fast says "wait".

## From sign-in to first diagram in a minute

Sign in

Use your Mermaid account at the console. Free accounts work.

Create a key

Name it after where it runs, like "CI" or "support bot".

Send your diagram

Diagram code, or a description of the diagram you want.

Get your answer

A verdict, an image, or working diagram code.

## From your program to your team

- Create and keep the ID

  Create a diagram in your default project or a chosen project. Keep the returned diagram ID to fetch or update it later.
- Open the editor

  Give a teammate the returned editUrl to open the diagram in Mermaid Chart with their existing permissions.
- Invite a collaborator

  Request a shareUrl when you want to invite someone. They must log in; invitations default to View, last 30 days and are not revocable before use.

[Stored-diagram docs](https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs#api-1/description/stored-diagrams)

## Valid, rendered, and ready to ship.

## FAQ

[Contact sales](https://mermaid.ai/contact-sales)

Mermaid is the open-source language and library that turns text into diagrams. Mermaid API is a hosted service that runs Mermaid for you: your program sends diagram code over HTTP and gets back a validation result, an image, or new diagram code.

No. Any Mermaid account works, including a free one, and every account gets a monthly allowance of API credits. Paid plans include a bigger allowance.

Costs depend on the operation and options; stored-diagram reads are free. Your monthly allowance is spent first, then any credits you have bought. See the current costs in [api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs](https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs); the free balance endpoint also returns your balance and endpoint costs. For high volume, contact sales.

Every diagram type Mermaid supports ([see the docs](https://mermaid.js.org)). Images come as SVG, PNG or PDF.

Validate, render, generate and repair do not save a diagram in Mermaid Chart. Create and update explicitly persist diagrams in Mermaid Chart; Mermaid API keeps no copy of the diagram code. Rendered images are cached for up to a day, and you can turn caching off per request. Usage records hold counts and sizes, never your diagrams.

Use a personal key: it can read, overwrite and share diagrams according to its owner's existing Mermaid Chart permissions, including team projects. Organisation keys cannot use stored-diagram operations. Trust key holders with that access and revoke keys you no longer trust. An editUrl opens the editor; it does not grant access. Edit URL access follows existing permissions; a share link invites a recipient to View, Comment or Edit. Each share request returns a new shareUrl. Recipients must log in; invitations default to View, last 30 days and are not revocable before use. You cannot grant more access than the key owner has. See [api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs](https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs) for the full contract.

Yes. Each call can name the Mermaid version it should use, so your output stays the same until you choose to upgrade.

Mermaid API is in open beta. You can build on it; breaking changes are announced in advance in the changelog, and there is no uptime guarantee yet.

At [api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs](https://api.mermaid.ai/v1/docs), with examples, an OpenAPI document and an llms.txt for agents.
